title: fcontour
summary: Plot contour lines of a scalar function.

gpu_support.notes: `fcontour` samples arbitrary function handles on the host, then uses RunMat's existing contour renderer. There is no provider callback kernel because MATLAB callbacks are not GPU kernels.

description: `fcontour` evaluates a function handle over a rectangular two-variable domain and renders contour lines from the sampled values.
behaviors: `fcontour(f, [xmin xmax ymin ymax])` uses an explicit rectangular domain; a two-element vector applies the same limits to both axes.
`fcontour(ax, ___)` renders into the requested axes and returns a function-contour graphics handle.
Function-handle outputs must be scalar real numeric values at every sampled point; non-finite samples are preserved as contour discontinuities.
Typed integer domain vectors, property scalars, and documented level vectors are accepted for all eight integer classes.
options: `'MeshDensity'` controls the number of samples along each domain dimension. RunMat accepts exact integer counts from 3 through the resource ceiling of 400.
`'LevelList'` accepts a nonempty real numeric row or column vector. An integer scalar selects one explicit level, and descending level order is accepted.
`'LevelStep'` accepts a nonnegative finite real numeric scalar. Zero selects automatic levels and a positive integer crosses one checked contour-geometry conversion boundary.
`'LineWidth'` accepts a positive finite real numeric scalar and crosses one checked renderer-property conversion boundary.
`'Fill'` accepts logical values or the exact numeric scalar values zero and one. One adds filled contour bands beneath the contour lines.
`'LineColor'` accepts the documented text forms. Typed-integer RGB is a separately gated RunMat extension; the undocumented `'Color'` alias is not accepted by `fcontour`.
`'DisplayName'` sets the function-contour graphics handle display name.
integer_semantics: `xyinterval` must be a two- or four-element row or column vector. Bounds are validated before the deliberate binary64 graphics-domain conversion.
All eight built-in integer classes are accepted for `xyinterval`, `MeshDensity`, `LevelList`, `LevelStep`, `LineWidth`, and numeric `Fill`.
Typed-integer `LineColor` and contour-style positional integer level specifications are RunMat extensions and are rejected unless RunMat extension mode is enabled.
Resident numeric arguments are also a RunMat extension; the compatibility gate runs before provider gathering.
compatibility_notes: RunMat currently invokes the callback once per sampled point. First-class function-contour object fidelity, matrix callback evaluation, symbolic expressions, and adaptive sampling remain deferred broader compatibility work.
The RunMat-only positional level shorthand is not part of the documented `fcontour` compatibility surface. Use `LevelList` or `LevelStep` for portable code.

faqs.question: Does `fcontour` evaluate the function handle on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. MATLAB function handles can contain arbitrary user code, so RunMat samples them on the host and then hands the sampled grid to the contour renderer.

faqs.question: What happens if the function returns a vector?
faqs.answer: RunMat raises `RunMat:fcontour:EvaluationFailed`; each sampled point must produce one scalar numeric value.

gpu_residency: `fcontour` is a callback-sampling builtin. It creates a new sampled contour plot and does not preserve input residency, because the input is a MATLAB function handle rather than a numeric provider buffer.
gpu_behavior: Callback sampling runs on the host.
The resulting contour uses the existing `runmat-plot` contour rendering path.
